title: 1974: the 1923 four-piece band and the Klan Kleagle
summary: Howard says Hawkins came in 1923 with Mamie Smith and Harvey Brooks, whom Howard hired for a four-piece band; he once had Lionel bailed out by a Klan Kleagle.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: I've seen pictures of, mahy pictures of you naturally, but things with Coleman Hawkins and things like that, how well did you know Hawkins?

Well, he came here in 1923, Coleman did, with Mamie Smith. He came with Harvey Brooks. I hired Harvey to play in our little four piece group. I said, "Do you want to get a little band together?" Harvey said, "Yes, I'd like to stay here." I said, "Okay, we'll organize a little band."

Four pieces, which we did. And that's when I got Leon, Harvey, Henry and myself. Harvey was -- Lionel was a very fine little young fellow, but he just would go off and get drunk, and chasing he white gals and get put in jail.
Huh? And get put in jail. Yeah, he'd get put in jail. And once George Orrendorf got -- George went with me, and you know what I did? I got the Kleagle of the Ku Klux Klan to get him out of jail.
Say that again. You got what?
The Kleagle of the Ku Klux Klan.
To get Orrendorf out or get Lionel?
Oh, no. Lionel. Oh, no. You going, Floyd?
Glad you stopped by. See you later.
Okay. See you later, bye, bye.
Excuse me. Can you get out? No, I don't want to talk in front of him. I didn't even want him here. No.
